questions.comparison_question_zh: 不同样品形态、取向、温度和回线饱和条件下，BFO 的自发极化报告为何不同？

source_candidates.title: Epitaxial BiFeO3 Multiferroic Thin Film Heterostructures
source_candidates.reported_lead: Room-temperature spontaneous polarization of about 50 to 60 uC/cm2.
source_candidates.claim_boundary: The value is film- and orientation-specific and does not by itself prove an intrinsic strain enhancement.

source_candidates.title: Very large spontaneous electric polarization in BiFeO3 single crystals at room temperature and its evolution under cycling fields
source_candidates.independence_note: Independent authors, institution, single-crystal route, and measurement campaign.
source_candidates.method_scope: Room-temperature electric polarization loops under cycling fields
source_candidates.reported_lead: Spontaneous polarization exceeds 100 uC/cm2 before cycling degradation prevents full saturation.
source_candidates.claim_boundary: High resistivity enables saturation; cycling degradation and crystallographic direction remain essential comparison fields.

source_candidates.title: Dielectric hysteresis in single crystal BiFeO3
source_candidates.independence_note: Independent early flux-growth and low-temperature measurement route.
source_candidates.sample_scope: Bi2O3-flux-grown single crystals measured in liquid nitrogen
source_candidates.method_scope: Unsaturated 60 Hz dielectric hysteresis loops with maximum field 55 kV/cm
source_candidates.reported_lead: Measured 3.5 uC/cm2 along 100, corresponding to 6.1 uC/cm2 along 111, at 77 K.
source_candidates.claim_boundary: The loops were explicitly unsaturated, so the low value is a measurement-boundary counterexample rather than an intrinsic bulk polarization.

questions.comparison_question_zh: BFO 薄膜的 R-like/T-like 相边界能否由单一失配应变决定，还是同时受厚度和温度控制？

source_candidates.title: A strain-driven morphotropic phase boundary in BiFeO3
source_candidates.independence_note: Primary report of the strain-driven mixed-phase route.
source_candidates.sample_scope: Epitaxial BiFeO3 films on highly compressive substrates
source_candidates.method_scope: Epitaxial growth, structural characterization, and electric-field phase conversion
source_candidates.reported_lead: R-like and T-like phase coexistence occurs near about -4.5 percent compressive strain.
source_candidates.claim_boundary: The approximate boundary is tied to substrate, thickness, and the monoclinic phase definitions used in the study.

source_candidates.title: Strain-driven phase boundaries in BiFeO3 thin films studied by atomic force microscopy and x-ray diffraction
source_candidates.independence_note: Independent film series and author group with AFM and XRD measurements.
source_candidates.sample_scope: Compressively strained epitaxial BiFeO3 films across thickness and temperature
source_candidates.method_scope: Atomic force microscopy and x-ray diffraction
source_candidates.reported_lead: T-like films have c/a near 1.2; high temperature and high strain favor the T-like phase, and an MC-to-MA transition is reported near 150 degC.
source_candidates.claim_boundary: The result directly makes thickness and temperature part of the phase boundary rather than treating strain as the only coordinate.

source_candidates.title: Large elasto-optic effect and reversible electrochromism in multiferroic BiFeO3
source_candidates.independence_note: Independent substrate series and diffraction analysis.
source_candidates.sample_scope: Fully strained films on substrates spanning about -7 to +1 percent mismatch
source_candidates.method_scope: Pulsed-laser deposition, x-ray diffraction, and reciprocal-space mapping
source_candidates.reported_lead: High compression at or beyond about -4 percent yields a T-like monoclinic phase with c/a about 1.26; all measured films remain monoclinic variants.
source_candidates.claim_boundary: A broad substrate series gives a related but not identical threshold and warns against relabelling T-like monoclinic films as a true tetragonal phase.

questions.comparison_question_zh: BFO 在约 820 至 930 摄氏度的结构相变和绝缘—金属指派是否被不同实验方法一致支持？

source_candidates.title: The beta-to-alpha transition in BiFeO3: a powder neutron diffraction study
source_candidates.sample_scope: Bulk powder BiFeO3 under variable temperature
source_candidates.method_scope: Powder neutron diffraction with phase coexistence analysis
source_candidates.reported_lead: First-order R3c-to-Pbnm ferroelectric transition across about 820 to 830 degC.
source_candidates.claim_boundary: Heating and cooling path, decomposition, and the high-temperature observation window must be retained.

source_candidates.title: Beta phase and gamma-beta metal-insulator transition in multiferroic BiFeO3
source_candidates.independence_note: Independent thin-film, crystal, and ceramic multi-method campaign.
source_candidates.sample_scope: Thin films, single crystals, and ceramics at high temperature
source_candidates.method_scope: Thermal analysis, Raman, x-ray diffraction, dc transport, and optical measurements
source_candidates.reported_lead: A beta region of about 820 to 925 degC and a gamma region beginning at 925 plus or minus 5 degC were reported with a metal-insulator interpretation.
source_candidates.claim_boundary: The multi-sample phase assignment must not be merged with neutron results without matching sample stability and decomposition conditions.

source_candidates.title: Phase transitions, electrical conductivity and chemical stability of BiFeO3 at high temperatures
source_candidates.independence_note: Independent calorimetry, dilatometry, conductivity, and oxygen-pressure study.
source_candidates.sample_scope: Bulk BiFeO3 under controlled high-temperature and oxygen-pressure conditions
source_candidates.method_scope: Calorimetry, dilatometry, electrical conductivity, and chemical-stability analysis
source_candidates.reported_lead: A first-order transition near 925 plus or minus 5 degC was observed, but the phase above it remained semiconducting rather than metallic.
source_candidates.claim_boundary: Oxygen partial pressure changes decomposition stability, directly limiting universal gamma-phase and metallic claims.

questions.comparison_question_zh: BFO 畴壁导电由哪些畴型、缺陷和热处理条件控制，哪些畴壁并不导电？

source_candidates.title: Conduction at domain walls in oxide multiferroics
source_candidates.independence_note: Primary thin-film c-AFM domain-wall conduction report.
source_candidates.sample_scope: Approximately 100 nm epitaxial BiFeO3 films with written 71, 109, and 180 degree walls
source_candidates.method_scope: PFM, conductive AFM, high-resolution TEM, and first-principles calculations
source_candidates.reported_lead: Current was in the pA regime at 109 and 180 degree walls, while 71 degree walls showed no conduction in that film route.
source_candidates.claim_boundary: Current depends on bias, tip contact, wall type, substrate, growth conditions, and time after writing; it is not an absolute bulk conductivity.

source_candidates.title: Domain-wall conduction in ferroelectric BiFeO3 controlled by accumulation of charged defects
source_candidates.independence_note: Independent polycrystalline sample route with atomic-scale chemistry.
source_candidates.sample_scope: Air-processed polycrystalline BiFeO3 with head-to-tail domain walls
source_candidates.method_scope: Atomic-resolution STEM and EELS with PFM and conductive AFM
source_candidates.reported_lead: Fe4+ and bismuth-vacancy accumulation supports p-type hopping conduction, tunable by annealing atmosphere.
source_candidates.claim_boundary: The identified defect mechanism is specific to the polycrystalline processing route and must not be generalized to every wall or film.

source_candidates.title: Domain-wall pinning and defect ordering in BiFeO3 probed on the atomic and nanoscale
source_candidates.independence_note: Follow-up group overlaps the 2017 ceramic route, so it is a boundary control rather than the independent support source.
source_candidates.sample_scope: Pristine, quenched, and aged polycrystalline BiFeO3; up to about 200 walls sampled per condition
source_candidates.method_scope: PFM, conductive AFM, STEM, EELS, controlled quenching, and slow-cooling aging
source_candidates.reported_lead: Quenching depletes mobile defects and greatly reduces the fraction of conductive walls; slow cooling restores a larger conductive fraction, and not every wall exceeds background.
source_candidates.claim_boundary: Conductive-wall fraction is thermal-history dependent, so a wall identity alone cannot determine conductivity.
